entry_conditions: Red is low or settled near the central buffer and may still be opening; blue is the intended object in the +y region. Two causal observations retained across a switch must distinguish blue from nearby red.
exit_conditions: Core exit is blue stationary inside the observed blue goal with gripper open and TCP clearing it. A later supported exit is buffered red aligned, closed on and beginning to lift while blue remains fixed at goal.
overlap_role: All assigned actions are supervised. Initial overlap covers final red lowering/release, retreat, complete blue approach, contact and lift; terminal overlap covers blue lowering/release, retreat, buffered-red approach, closure and initial lift.
successor_readiness: Switch to place_red once blue is visibly settled in the blue goal and the gripper is open/clear, or through the later overlap once buffered red follows the closed gripper upward. A close command alone is not proof of grasp.
failure_signatures: Wrong-object approach, buffered red movement, blue not following a closed gripper, release outside goal, blue remaining attached, or repeated IK nonconvergence. Route a held blue near destination to h02 and modest intermediate TCP offsets to h03.
continuation_guidance: Replan the blue frame from current observations for each new chunk; keep it fixed only across that chunk. Continue through overlap when semantic switch cues are not yet met, but stop on object-identity ambiguity, visible loss of blue, red disturbance or persistent IK residuals.
limitations: Observed successful trajectories do not demonstrate recovery from drops, wrong-object grasps, collisions or unreachable displacements. Object-relative geometry preserves relationships but not contact, collision, or reach feasibility.
